title: Drop raw footage in a folder and a Claude Code skill returns an edited video
summary: Browser Use's open-source video-use skill has Claude Code inventory clips, propose an edit plan, then cut filler words, grade color, add subtitles and render a final MP4 using transcripts and on-demand frame snapshots.
agent_role: The agent plans and executes the edit with ffmpeg and ElevenLabs transcription; the user describes the edit and approves the plan before rendering.
what_they_did: Browser Use released video-use, an open-source skill that lets Claude Code or another shell-capable agent edit video. You point the agent at a folder of raw takes and describe the edit, for example 'edit these into a launch video'. The agent transcribes each clip with ElevenLabs Scribe and reads the word-level transcript. It looks at filmstrip and waveform images only at decision points. It proposes a strategy and waits for approval. Then it cuts filler words and dead space, grades color, burns in subtitles and renders with ffmpeg.
worth_knowing: The model never watches the video. It works from a roughly 12KB transcript plus a few PNG snapshots instead of thousands of frames. It also checks every cut in the render and re-renders up to three times before showing you a preview. You need an ElevenLabs API key and ffmpeg.
prompt: Set up https://github.com/browser-use/video-use for me. Read install.md, install ffmpeg and dependencies, register the skill, and ask me for my ElevenLabs API key when needed. Then read SKILL.md and helpers/. When I drop footage into [folder path], inventory the clips. Propose an edit plan for [describe the video you want, e.g. a 60-second launch video], including cuts, color grade style and subtitle style. Wait for my approval before cutting or rendering. Then produce edit/final.mp4.
